children: Hubble Network raised $200 million in a Series C round that valued the Seattle-based satellite Bluetooth startup at $1.6 billion, as it opened its constellation to general availability on Wednesday.
The round was led by Smith Point Capital, with participation from Seraphim, Carthona Capital, Earthshot Ventures, Y Combinator and RPM Ventures.

The financing brings Hubble's total funding to $300 million. The company said it would use the new capital to expand its satellite constellation to 60 satellites by 2030, from six currently operating in low Earth orbit.

Hubble said its technology enables standard Bluetooth Low Energy radios already inside a device to transmit location and sensor data globally through a firmware update, without cellular modems, GPS or dedicated satellite hardware.
Hubble said it has partnerships with semiconductor company Texas Instruments
, and said smart-label maker Reelables is also working with the company.
Hubble was founded by Alex Haro, who previously co-founded Life360, a location-based connectivity company that allows families to share their locations.
